The core insight is that consensus odds, interpreted as inverse mean of bookmaker prices, approximate true probability through the wisdom-of-crowds principle. The betting rule selects when individual bookies offer odds exceeding this consensus-adjusted fair value, adjusted by a margin α. This creates a binary decision process: bet if max(odds) > 1/(p*(1-α)). The mathematical duality lies between the probabilistic consensus and the decision boundary. Failure modes include stale odds (reducing signal validity), selection bias (skewing sample), and asymmetric margins (distorting inversion). The model assumes symmetric margins and executable quotes, which may not hold in practice. The empirical evaluation shows marginal statistical significance (p=0.089) but consistent positive returns under realistic simulations, suggesting robustness despite theoretical limitations.
